evidence_items.publisher: The Register (reporting Lucidworks 2024 Generative AI Global Benchmark Study)

receipt.public_excerpt: There are also many more worries (5x more) about the accuracy of responses provided by AI systems.

evidence_items.explanation: The survey ran April-May 2024. It finds companies more cautious than in 2023 (63% plan to raise AI spending versus 93%), and worries about response accuracy up fivefold. This supports a cooling with unreliability as one named cause. The sample is companies with 100+ employees, not just the Fortune 500.

evidence_items.publisher: The Register (reporting Lucidworks 2024 Generative AI Global Benchmark Study)

receipt.public_excerpt: 63 percent of global companies plan to increase spending on AI in the next twelve months, compared to 93 percent in 2023

evidence_items.explanation: Shows the size of the cooling in spending plans after the 2023 hype. Most firms still planned to increase spending.

receipt.public_excerpt: Though these leaders still have some reservations about deploying generative AI, they’re also nearly tripling their budgets, expanding the number of use cases that are deployed on smaller open-source models, and transitioning more workloads from early experimentation into production.

evidence_items.explanation: In early 2024 interviews, Fortune 500 and top enterprise leaders were nearly tripling LLM budgets and moving workloads into production. That cuts against a general loss of confidence among Fortune 500 firms. The source is an AI investor with an interest in the outcome.

receipt.public_excerpt: 2 primary concerns about genAI still loom large in the enterprise: 1) potential issues with hallucination and safety

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms hallucination (reliability) was a leading enterprise concern that limited customer-facing deployment, even as budgets grew.

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI said 92 per cent of Fortune 500 companies are using its products

evidence_items.explanation: A vendor claim of broad Fortune 500 usage a month after the post. It is outside the target period and does not measure depth of use, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: No survey found that measures confidence specifically among Fortune 500 firms over 2023-2024.
The share of any cooling caused by reliability, versus cost, security and unclear ROI, is not measured.
The primary Lucidworks report could not be read (HTTP 403). It is cited through The Register.
